messages:
alex: heads up — ops noticed a spike in websocket reconnects around 03:12 UTC, clients report partial frames and then immediate reconnects. seen across two routes.
sam: logs show a TON of `ping_timeout` errors from the edge layer. our ws-proxy sent pings but clients never ACKed, proxy then force-closes.
lee: is this the same keepalive change we rolled last week to reduce idle sockets?
alex: that change only applied to SSE canary. these are websocket routes, different config.
irene: telemetry shows reconnects are concentrated on routes using the new regional routing policy (sticky=false). could be a routing flip causing mid-flight proxy hops.
sam: if a connection gets proxied mid-stream we might lose the client-inflight ACK race. gateway expects pongs within 10s; proxy sometimes inserts an extra hop with a 2s stall.
lee: we should try to correlate `proxy_hop_count` tag with `ws_reconnect` metric. currently console panels don't show hop_count next to reconnects, only in raw traces.
irene: agree — add `proxy_hop_count` as a dimension on the reconnect dashboard. also add `route_policy` label (sticky|stateless) so PMs can see effect of policy flips.
alex: operationally, do we want to treat reconnects from hop_count>1 as non-resume? clients resume flow expects KV cache continuity, which breaks if we bounced across proxies.
sam: non-resume would prevent confused resume acceptance and duplicate billing, but would increase fresh session opens. Could be costly.
lee: middle ground: if hop_count > 1 but client provided a resume token and our cache still has the session, allow resume; otherwise force fresh. we need a cheap cache validation check — maybe a quick PK lookup for session_id.
irene: we'd also benefit from a new telemetry tag `resume_validation:{none,quick,full}` to track how many resumes required the validation. surface that in console and annotate rollouts.
ops-bot: alert: ws_reconnect_rate exceeded 0.8% on route: /v1/streaming/chat-region-eu at 03:15 UTC.
alex: rolling plan — short-term: 1) add hop_count header emitted by edge-proxy when routing hops >1 (flagged off). 2) wire hop_count as metric tag in gateway. 3) update console dashboard to show reconnect_rate split by hop_count and route_policy. 4) change resume logic to do quick validation on hop_count>1 (feature-flag).
sam: for safety, quick validation should be idempotent and cheap: do a single KV probe `cache.peek(session_id)` with 5ms timeout. If probe times out, treat as non-resume.
lee: also we should add an audit trace when resume accepted after hop_count>1 for a short period so oncall can inspect possible duplicated billing cases.
irene: UX note: in rollout page, add an expected delta panel that predicts fresh_session_rate change when switching sticky->stateless using historical traffic. PMs requested that in the last ship review.
alex: timeline? can we get hop_count header in a proxy canary in 3 hours?
sam: yes, I can open PR now and gate it behind `feature.hop_count_header`.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: edge-proxy-canary-24 -> canary-cluster (manual approval required).
irene: i'll prototype the dashboard panel and the KV quick-check today. want the metric to be available before we flip any routes.
lee: one more thought — update billing instrumentation to attach `resume_path` (`direct`,`proxied`,`reconstructed`) so finance can filter duplicates quickly.
alex: good call. add `resume_path` to telemetry plan and map proxied resumes to an experimental label until we have confidence.
sam: follow-up ticket: add e2e smoke test that simulates proxy hop injection and verifies client sees pings/pongs and resume behavior. I'll link tests in PR.
irene: approved to proceed on the dashboard + metric ingestion. will coordinate with oncall for an observation window after canary.
alex: thanks all — let's aim to have quick-val resume logic and hop_count header merged and canaried before EOD. keep me posted in the ticket thread. :eyes:
